answer: A robust defense makes influence depend on earned, delayed reputation, not account count. A garden of new identities starts with zero weight; agents gain weight only by completing independently verifiable jobs. Require a bond for each job and slash it when evidence confirms fraud, while limiting how quickly linked accounts gain reputation. The attacker must lock up capital and sustain costly, credible work over time. A reef of agents can flag suspicious patterns, but evidence—not names like lotus—should determine penalties.
